ingredients.name: King coconut (thambili)
ingredients.notes: a whole, fresh king coconut; the orange-shelled variety (Cocos nucifera var. aurantiaca) endemic to Sri Lanka. Choose one that sounds full of water when shaken. A mature thambili has less water but slightly sweeter; a young one has more water and lighter sweetness.

ingredients.name: Lime
ingredients.notes: optional; a small squeeze enhances the natural sweetness of the water

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: optional; a pinch of salt is a traditional addition by some vendors, as it balances electrolytes and enhances flavour -- particularly recommended as a post-exercise drink

steps.instruction: Have a vendor or experienced person open the king coconut using a large sharp knife or machete: hold the thambili firmly on a stable surface and make 4-5 angled chops around the top to create a pentagon-shaped opening. Alternatively, use a specialised thambili opener. Take care -- the shell is very hard and the cutting requires skill and a sharp blade.
Once opened, the water is ready to drink directly from the shell with a straw. Optionally add a squeeze of lime juice and a pinch of salt to the water inside and stir with the straw before drinking.

After drinking all the water, use a piece of the cut shell as a makeshift spoon to scoop out the thin, jelly-like king coconut flesh (which is softer and more delicate than regular coconut flesh) and eat it directly. This is considered the best part by many Sri Lankans.

source_site: serendipdelights.com, cross-checked against lakpura.com, ceylonheritage.lk, Wikipedia (Thambili), joyofeatingtheworld.com, foodcnr.com, and backtonature.lk
collection_method: scraped, cross-checked across 7+ independent sources; highest trust score in the entire collection -- the recipe cannot be simpler, and sourcing is perfectly consistent
notes: Thambili (king coconut) is Sri Lanka's most iconic drink and most immediately recognisable symbol of the island -- the bright orange coconuts sold by roadside vendors are a ubiquitous sight from Colombo to Jaffna. King coconuts are a variety endemic to Sri Lanka (Cocos nucifera var. aurantiaca) and are botanically and commercially distinct from the regular brown coconut -- the water is sweeter, more electrolyte-rich, and considered more medicinally valuable in traditional practice. This entry has the highest trust score in the entire SL-Cook100 dataset (0.97) because the recipe is essentially just 'open a coconut and drink it' -- there is no meaningful technique variation across sources. The gentle lime-and-salt addition is optional but widely practised, especially by athletes and those using it as a rehydration drink. The soft inner flesh (thambili pani pol) that lines the shell after drinking is equally prized and is sometimes used in desserts.
